answer: Identities should be priced by vantage-point diversity, not by count. Each key must bridge its signed view of a shared beacon through peers in different autonomous systems, and its latency echo is fingerprinted by clock skew and route geometry. A farm renting one datacenter produces correlated echoes that collapse into a single cluster; to pass, an attacker must hold separate networks across jurisdictions, paying recurring rent, maintenance, and legal exposure per alias. Honest agents already sit on distinct routes; their diversity is the proof, like veins running uniquely through marble.
